children: Italian borrowing costs spiked at an auction on Thursday, ahead of an ECB meeting expected to hike rates.
The Rome-based Treasury sold the top planned amount of €7.75 billion ($9.02 billion) in three BTP bonds.
The Treasury placed €3.5 billion of a 3-year BTP bond due in September 2029 with a 3.43% yield, the highest level since June 2024, versus 2.98% at the previous auction in mid-July.
A 7-year BTP bond - allotted for €3.5 billion - fetched a 3.98% gross yield, the highest since November 2023, compared with 3.50% two months ago.
Rome also placed €750 million of a 50-year BTP at a 4.61% gross yield. The previous 50-year auction dates back to May 2024.
